extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, media innovators, news startups, and readers interested in the future of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: An 'About' page describing the Nieman Journalism Lab's mission to study and promote ways quality journalism can survive and thrive in the Internet age, including research, coverage of innovation, and collaborations with academic centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlight attempts at innovation and analyze success/failure
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want to highlight attempts at innovation and figure out what makes them succeed or fail."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus coverage on specific innovative efforts in journalism and analyze the factors that lead to their success or failure; use case studies and reporting to surface causes and lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and surface replicable ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want to find good ideas for others to steal."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize ideas and practices that are practical and transferable to other newsrooms; emphasize clear descriptions of implementation so others can adopt them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help reporters and editors adjust to online labors
rubrics_metrics.description: "We want to help reporters and editors adjust to their online labors;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide guidance, resources, and coverage aimed at equipping journalists and editors with skills, workflows, and practices suited to online reporting and publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and promote sustainable business models for traditional news organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: "we want to help traditional news organizations find a way to survive;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate, analyze, and explain new business model options and strategies that could enable legacy news organizations to remain viable in the Internet era; include partnerships with business research (e.g., Harvard Business School).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support coverage and assessment of news startups
rubrics_metrics.description: "we want to help the new crop of startups that will complement — or supplant — them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover emerging media startups, assess their approaches and potential impacts, and consider how they interact with or replace traditional news institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster collaborative reader contributions and community input
rubrics_metrics.description: "Primary among them are our readers; we hope your contributions will make the Lab a collaborative exchange of ideas. Tell us what's happening around you, or what should be."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reader-submitted tips, local observations, and participation to inform reporting and shape the Lab's coverage; treat the audience as active contributors to the project's knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use interdisciplinary partnerships to study journalism's future
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lab works with the Harvard Business School on new business models, the Berkman Center for Internet and Society on understanding online life, and the Hauser Center for Nonprofit Organizations on one potential path for news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine business, internet-society, and nonprofit perspectives when evaluating journalism experiments and models; draw on academic research and cross-disciplinary expertise to inform assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote and document quality journalism in changing contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Nieman Journalism Lab is a collaborative attempt to figure out how quality journalism can survive and thrive in the Internet age."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame work around sustaining 'quality journalism'—document threats, innovations, and practical steps to maintain journalistic standards amid technological and business changes.
